# KBD Constraints — flint-realtime-fabric

> The canonical constraint set the per-change QA gate validates against. Read by
> `/kbd-execute`'s QA step (and the `qa-gate.sh` helper) after a change reaches DONE,
> before archive. Source of truth: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PROMETHEUS-BASE-RULES.md`, and
> `~/.claude/rules/rust/*`. Severity drives the gate: **BLOCKING** fails the change
> (→ mark BLOCKED + refine); HIGH/MEDIUM are reported but do not block.

## Legend

- **BLOCKING** — a violation fails the QA gate; the change is marked BLOCKED in
  `progress.json` and must be refined before archive.
- **HIGH / MEDIUM** — reported in the refinement log; reviewed, not auto-blocking.

---

## Architecture (BLOCKING)

- **A1 — Dependency direction.** Nothing in `frf-domain` or `frf-app`/`frf-ports` may
  import an adapter crate (`frf-broker-*`, `frf-authz-*`, `frf-store-*`, `frf-media-*`,
  `frf-bridge-*`, `frf-identity-*`, `frf-policy-*`, `frf-crdt`, `frf-postgres-cdc`).
  Composition happens only in `frf-gateway`.
  *Check:* the `[dependencies]` of `frf-domain` and `frf-app` contain no adapter crate.
- **A2 — One port per adapter.** Each `frf-*` adapter implements exactly one port trait
  and does not reach into another adapter crate.
- **A3 — Proto is frozen.** No edit to `proto/flint/v1/*.proto` (frozen at `proto-v1`).
  A wire-breaking change is a NEW proto version. Non-Rust SDKs generate from the source
  proto — no forked copy committed under `sdks/`.

## Rust quality gates (BLOCKING)

- **R1 — Compiles.** `cargo check --workspace` is clean.
- **R2 — Clippy.** `cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic`
  is clean, plus the `--features frf-gateway/dev-endpoints` and `--tests` passes.
- **R3 — No library `unwrap()`/`expect()`.** `clippy::unwrap_used` / `expect_used` are
  denied at the workspace level; they are allowed only in tests (`clippy.toml`). `anyhow`
  only at binary edges (`frf-gateway`, `frf-cli`).
- **R4 — Formatted.** `cargo fmt --check --all` is clean.
- **R5 — File size.** No hand-authored file over **500 lines** (any language or
  format). Split into a directory module when approaching it. Machine-generated
  dependency lockfiles are exempt because their package managers require the
  native single-file format; do not split or hand-edit them for line count.

## Rust idioms (HIGH)

- **I1 — `#[non_exhaustive]`** on public enums.
- **I2 — Newtype IDs** (`#[repr(transparent)]`) over bare `String` for entity IDs.
- **I3 — `tracing` spans** across every port-boundary call.
- **I4 — MSRV pinned** in the workspace manifest; semver discipline on `frf-domain` and
  SDK crates.

## Security (BLOCKING)

- **S1 — No hardcoded secrets** (API keys, tokens, signing secrets) in any committed
  file. Secrets come from env / a secret manager; validated present at startup.
- **S2 — No auth bypass in a release artifact.** `DEV_NO_AUTH` / `dev-endpoints` are
  compiled out of the production image; never enabled in `compose.yml`.
- **S3 — No sensitive logging.** Never log JWT payloads, relation tuples, or tenant
  identifiers as credentials. (`tenant_id` as a structured observability field is OK.)
- **S4 — Tenant isolation** is enforced at Keto plus the app-layer tenant-equality guard;
  never trust unverified claims downstream.

## Tests & docs (HIGH)

- **T1 — Tests for new behavior.** New logic carries unit/integration tests (AAA); target
  80%+ where practical. Live-service tests gate on env vars and skip cleanly when unset.
- **T2 — Honest surface.** No "healthy but does nothing": a plane/endpoint is either
  functional or explicitly labeled unimplemented/deferred. No doc drift — docs match code.

## Frontend / TypeScript (BLOCKING where the change touches `admin-ui/` or `sdks/ts`)

- **F1 — No `any` types.** TSX over JSX. Components render; hooks coordinate; stores own
  state; services call APIs — no component fetches data directly.

## Spec-backend hygiene (BLOCKING for OpenSpec changes)

- **P1 — Valid spec delta.** Each change carries a `specs/<capability>/spec.md` delta
  (`## ADDED/MODIFIED/...` + a MUST/SHALL body line + `#### Scenario:` blocks) so
  `openspec validate <id>` passes before archive.

---

## Per-change applicability

Not every constraint applies to every change. The gate evaluates the subset relevant to
the files a change touched:

| Change kind | BLOCKING subset |
|-------------|-----------------|
| Rust code | A1–A3, R1–R5, S1–S4, P1 |
| Config / compose | S1, S2, P1 |
| Docs-only | T2 (no drift), P1 |
| Frontend / TS | F1, R5 (size), P1 |
| Tooling / KBD | P1 |

# Diagnose and reduce the existing ASO replica memory cost

## Why

Assessment and analysis for production-readiness-integration identify an unmet
integration gate in C08. This change supplies one bounded
acceptance slice; implementation and production qualification remain separate.

## What Changes

Reconcile current source with mounted receipts and profile the existing 16203-row workload. Apply measured, bounded memory corrections while preserving SQL/checkpoint atomicity, owner fencing and the experimental gate.

## Ownership and Dependencies

Owner: ASO materializer + PEM. Depends on: pri-c002-local-fixtures, pri-c003-scope-research-contract.
Decision inputs before product implementation: Q7.
Status: proposal only; all implementation tasks are unchecked.

## Impact

Affected modules and repository-relative paths:
- `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/TribeHealth/kevin/prior-auth/web/src/shared/sync/`
- `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/TribeHealth/kevin/prior-auth/scripts/test-ra11c-materialization.py`

Dependency-rule impact: keep domain/application imports inward; adapter behavior
is accessed through ports, with one port per adapter and gateway composition.
Changes to public domain/port types require a documented semver decision.

## Foundation Compatibility

Preserve the completed Phase 0 foundation: workspace build and immutable v1
contract. This is a readiness follow-up; it does not recreate or claim Phase 0.

## Non-goals

Unrelated refactoring, automatic production deployment/publication, and KBD
runtime migration are outside this proposal. Full readiness requires the phase's
other accepted gates; this slice cannot certify them.

# pri-c014 acceptance B — allocation explanation

Result: **Passed**  
Observed: 2026-09-17T12:56:56.357614Z  
Dataset: 16,203 synthetic rows  
Campaign: `allocation-profile-campaign.json`  
Campaign SHA-256: `cb84c4b5eb3694f1dd0bedffd78e5baf90b3eccd3025fdcdf9d34e6c0d4b7476`

## Outcome

The current ASO materializer completed the full authenticated
PostgreSQL → Kratos → Gate → Fabric → Electric → PGlite → PEM campaign with
444,743,680 incremental RSS bytes and 62,831,744 incremental heap bytes. The
fixed limits are 536,870,912 RSS bytes and 268,435,456 heap bytes. All eleven
behavior assertions and all cleanup assertions passed after stage profiling was
added.

The historical current-fixture receipt measured 1,016,692,736 incremental RSS
bytes. The current result is 571,949,056 bytes lower, a 56.26% reduction. The
measured source uses a versioned PGlite base archive, 128 MiB initial WASM
memory, bounded PostgreSQL settings, 100-row SQL statements, and 500-row graph
projection reads.

## Allocation profile

The memory test sampled the same process at explicit boundaries. Deltas are
relative to the preceding boundary.

| Boundary | RSS delta | Heap delta | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| PGlite open | +376,307,712 | +23,691,400 | WASM filesystem/database startup dominates the process. |
| Schema setup | +30,375,936 | +4,547,800 | Replica tables, ledger, and PGlite schema initialization. |
| Empty graph and projector | +3,719,168 | +846,448 | Graph runtime and projector before any entity rows exist. |
| Electric cold fold complete | +27,852,800 | -13,761,096 | Net sample after seven shape buffers become one revision. V8 collected response intermediates before the boundary, so the negative heap delta is not treated as negative allocation. |
| SQL, checkpoint, projection, graph publication | +6,324,224 | +45,934,712 | Transactional writes, paged SQL readback, and retained PEM graph state. |
| Final settling | +163,840 | +1,572,480 | Count assertions and final report serialization. |

PGlite open plus schema setup accounts for 406,683,648 bytes, or 91.44% of
incremental RSS. At the measured peak, 381,911,936 incremental RSS bytes are
outside V8's reported heap. That relationship, together with the PGlite-open
boundary, identifies the embedded database/WASM runtime as the dominant
allocation surface. JavaScript cold-fold and graph state remain bounded by the
62,831,744-byte heap high-water increase.

## Worker and owner allocation

`ReplicaWorkerOwner` is a Web Locks lifecycle owner that may run inside a tab
or worker. It does not construct another `Worker` or another database. Its
resource factory owns the single PGlite handle and closes it before replacement
ownership can proceed.

The durable continuation process sampled immediately before and after owner
replacement. The upper bound for replacement ownership plus its final revision
was 4,521,984 RSS bytes and 4,245,984 heap bytes. This is deliberately reported
as an upper bound because the interval also includes the replacement revision;
the owner object alone cannot be isolated from that required work. The complete
continuation process stayed below the budget at 363,282,432 incremental RSS and
100,131,952 incremental heap bytes.

## Why the correction works

The current correction has four source mechanisms:

1. `pglite-bootstrap.ts` loads a versioned empty archive instead of running a
   second in-process `initdb`, starts with 128 MiB, and configures 32 MiB shared
   buffers plus small work, maintenance, temporary, and WAL buffers.
2. `frf-shape-transport.ts` folds cold Electric messages by primary key in
   response order, emits one coherent revision, and clears the cold maps before
   returning it.
3. `chunk-writer.ts` writes at most 100 rows per SQL statement, preventing one
   several-thousand-parameter WASM allocator high-water mark.
4. `replica-runtime.ts` reads graph projections in 500-row pages and publishes
   only after rows and the complete checkpoint commit atomically.

The memory correction preserves the experimental materializer gate. No default
production adoption flag changed.

## Behavior after optimization

The profiled campaign passed:

- initial SQL/graph parity and complete shape checkpoint;
- canonical gate-summary publication and reference identities;
- cold-start and captured-revision rollback without partial state;
- process restart without skipped committed SQL;
- delete-triggered replacement;
- disposed-owner fencing and replacement-owner continuation;
- authority-failure publication and pre-checkpoint fencing;
- synthetic rows, identity, PGlite store, service, and callback cleanup.

TypeScript and oxlint also exited zero after instrumentation. The two modified
ASO files contain 411 and 361 lines. The pre-existing 524-line
`replica-runtime.ts` and 659-line `replica-runtime.test.ts` were inspected but
not modified.
